before.con-physics-does-not-exhaust-matter: Because scientific descriptions model behavior without exhausting ontology, unknown properties of matter remain possible and Kastrup’s quantitative definition cannot establish impossibility.
before.pro-shared-world-is-transpersonal-experi: External reality consists of transpersonal experiential states that resist personal control because dissociation separates them, appearing materially across the resulting boundary.
before.pro-metabolism-marks-tentative-boundary: Kastrup tentatively correlates dissociation with metabolism, extending possible consciousness to the simplest metabolizing organism while excluding viruses that lack independent metabolism.

after.con-physics-does-not-exhaust-matter: Because scientific descriptions capture measurable behavior without exhausting matter’s ontology, unknown properties remain possible; therefore, Kastrup’s quantitative account cannot prove qualitative emergence impossible.
after.pro-shared-world-is-transpersonal-experi: Because dissociation makes transpersonal experiential states resist personal control and appear material across its boundary, they parsimoniously explain the shared external world without an ontological abyss.
after.pro-metabolism-marks-tentative-boundary: Because metabolism is uniquely distinctive and correlates with dissociation, Kastrup tentatively places consciousness at the simplest metabolizing organisms, thereby excluding nonmetabolizing viruses.
